rationale:
Evidence: iteration 7 (sensor_size 0.012, raced 58.1734) is the best raced design. Iteration 9 showed that shrinking the footprint to 0.008 lowers the score to 55.13, so smaller footprints are worse. Iterations 7 and 8 gave identical scores, so kd, wheel_track and base_speed have no measurable effect in this regime.

What I accepted from the round-2 critique: the change is attributable only if one variable moves from the raced baseline, so I keep sensor_size as the only change. I also accept that the proposed mechanism is untested and that the two oval line-loss events have persisted across layout, gain, footprint and speed changes. That points to a fixed early cause, such as the seeded motor mismatch or the start transient, not to the footprint.

What I rejected or changed: the critique says the line-loss and progress targets do not discriminate. I accept that and drop them as success criteria. I keep the reversal rule because it is clear and reproducible with fixed seeds. I do not change the controller or geometry to address the motor mismatch in this race, because that would confound the sensor test again. I will note it as the next candidate cause.

What I changed: nothing relative to my revision. The design keeps sensor_size 0.016 with the iteration 7 controller and geometry. I expect the score to move only slightly. If the larger footprint blurs the edge reading, s-bend and slalom max_error should rise. If it keeps more reading sum when the edge falls between sensors, oval line_loss_events should fall. I predict the score stays within about 1 point of 58.17 with no large change on any track.

Reversal rule: if the score falls below 58.17, or any track's max_error rises above its raced value (oval 0.0652, s-bend 0.0665, slalom 0.0624), the final stage uses sensor_size 0.012 with the iteration 7 design as the fallback.
